result.summary: G1, G2, G3, F-1, F-2, F-3 are resolved. G1: literal TASK_WORKER rule via Scope.allowed_for_role?/3 and allowed_set_for_role/2 (C.3, D9, T-F15, T-F16, MU36); assign/reassign on the route permission; the wider reading stays OQ-3. G2: Catalog rule 11 admits an unmanaged declaration only for a module on a config/test.exs-only allowlist, ScopeDeclaration repeats the check (defence in depth), T-D8 scans config and lib, R-3 restated, R-7 corrected to say tenant_wide is not restrictive-only, R-8 added, OQ-1/OQ-4 closed for production. G3: 2c-i-a / 2c-i-b split with consistent section 1, 3.1, 7.1, 9, 10 tables; 2d five-commit order (C.0) with only commit 4 changing route classes; snapshot arithmetic 0 + 4(+2) + 15 + 7 = 28 holds with M2/H1 declared in 2c-i-b. F-1: telemetry event [:letflow,:scope,:not_found] with closed metadata and T-W19. F-2: 5.5 create short-circuits before the multipart read, MU38/T-W20; mutants renamed MU. F-3: OQ-8 states the committed-write caveat. Findings (non-blocking, fixed or recorded): the G1 tenant-wide exemption widens AC 13's 'iff' and needed an RA entry (added RA-13); stale 2c-i labels fixed; 2c-i-a sizing under the threading default recorded.

independent_verification.exemption_check: C.3 (1): a principal for whom Scope.allowed?(principal, route_permission, :tenant_wide) allows is exempt from the grant requirement and keeps today's behavior plus the routing-role checks. This does not contradict AC 13 cases (a)-(e) or D9/Q3 for scoped callers and matches D1 (tenant-wide on a permission is tenant-wide), including the mixed scoped TASK_WORKER + tenant-wide PROCESS_OPERATOR case (T-F15). It does extend AC 13's literal 'iff TASK_WORKER grant' to a tenant-wide PROCESS_OPERATOR/TENANT_ADMIN without that grant, who is still bound by the routing-role rule. Not a defect, but it must be visible to REQ-ANALYST and SEC: recorded as RA-13.
